analysis.evidence: אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה forms the numeral ‘fourteen’. With שָׁנָה ‘year’, the phrase dates Chedorlaomer’s arrival to the fourteenth year.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means ‘and’. The preposition בְּ marks time (‘in’). אַרְבַּע is a feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral forming a compound with עֶשְׂרֵה.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 69124:1, 68377:7, 67348:1, 66826:7, 66824:5.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral, the second element of the compound numeral שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה.
analysis.sense: ten, in the numbers eleven to nineteen

analysis.evidence: וּבְאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה means “and in the fourteenth year.” It dates the arrival of Chedorlaomer and the kings with him.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state, following the compound numeral אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה (fourteen).
analysis.sense: year of a reign or era (in dates)

analysis.evidence: The verse dates the arrival of Chedorlaomer and the kings with him to the fourteenth year. The following plural verb וַיַּכּוּ, “and they struck,” recounts what they did after they came.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular. The verb precedes the compound subject and agrees with its first member, כְדָרְלָעֹמֶר.

analysis.evidence: בָּא כְדָרְלָעֹמֶר names the person who came. In וְהַמְּלָכִים אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ, “and the kings who were with him,” the singular suffix on אִתּוֹ refers back to Chedorlaomer.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The initial כ is part of the name.
analysis.sense: The personal name of the king who came with the other kings.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ identifies these kings as the rulers accompanying Chedorlaomer. The plural verb וַיַּכּוּ describes their joint action with him.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ means “and,” the definite article הַ means “the,” and מְּלָכִים is a masculine plural absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ, “who were with him,” which modifies הַמְּלָכִים, “the kings.” The suffix on אִתּוֹ refers to Chedorlaomer.
analysis.morphology: Indeclinable Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The repeated direct-object marker אֶת introduces three peoples, the Rephaim, the Zuzim, and the Emim. Each is named with the place where the kings defeated them during their campaign.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural. The plural subject is Chedorlaomer and the kings with him.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּכּוּ אֶת רְפָאִים, אֶת marks רְפָאִים (the Rephaim) as the people the kings struck. The marker recurs before the two other groups they struck, הַזּוּזִים and הָאֵימִים.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Append the gentilic as word 4 and retain the existing noun for the dead at word 3.
draft.definition: Rephaim is a designation for an ancient people. Genesis names them among the peoples defeated by Chedorlaomer and his allies.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:5 names the Rephaim as a military opponent at Ashteroth-karnaim. Deuteronomy 2:10–11 says that the people whom the Moabites called Emim were reckoned among the Rephaim.

analysis.evidence: After וַיַּכּוּ, “they struck,” אֶת marks רְפָאִים as the first people defeated. The verse pairs each people with the place of its defeat, beginning with the Rephaim at Ashteroth-karnaim and continuing with the Zuzim at Ham and the Emim at Shaveh-kiriathaim.
analysis.morphology: Gentilic noun, masculine plural absolute. The ending ־ִים marks the plural. The word has no prefix or pronominal suffix.

draft.change: Add a place-name entry for עַשְׁתְּרֹת under its own consonants. The verse establishes its use as a name but supplies no verbal derivation.
draft.definition: Ashteroth is the first element of Ashteroth-karnaim, where the kings struck the Rephaim.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:5 pairs each people struck with the place of its defeat. The place given for the Rephaim is עַשְׁתְּרֹת קַרְנַיִם.

analysis.evidence: וַיַּכּוּ אֶת רְפָאִים identifies the Rephaim as the people the kings struck. בְּעַשְׁתְּרֹת קַרְנַיִם gives the location, just as בְּהָם gives the location where they struck the Zuzim.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition בְּ means “at.” It attaches to עַשְׁתְּרֹת, the first element of the place name עַשְׁתְּרֹת קַרְנַיִם.
analysis.sense: Ashteroth in the place name Ashteroth-karnaim

analysis.evidence: בְּעַשְׁתְּרֹת קַרְנַיִם names the place where the kings struck the Rephaim. The locative בְּ on עַשְׁתְּרֹת governs the full name Ashteroth-karnaim, just as בְּהָם identifies where they struck the Zuzim.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with the dual ending ־ַיִם. It has no prefix or pronominal suffix.

draft.change: Append the plural gentilic זוּזִים as word 1 under זוז. Its historical relationship to זִיז is uncertain.
draft.definition: The Zuzim, a people defeated at Ham by Chedorlaomer and his allies.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:5 names the Zuzim between the Rephaim and the Emim in a list of peoples defeated by the kings.

analysis.evidence: וְאֶת marks הַזּוּזִים as an object of וַיַּכּוּ, “they struck,” and בְּהָם locates their defeat at Ham. The surrounding clauses likewise name the Rephaim and the Emim and give the place where each people was struck.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial ז of the gentilic noun זוּזִים. The ending ־ִים is masculine plural, and the noun is in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: The people whom Chedorlaomer and his allies defeated at Ham.

draft.change: Add הָם as a place name under its own consonants. The verse gives no evidence for a verbal derivation.
draft.definition: Ham is the place where Chedorlaomer and the kings with him struck the Zuzim.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 14:5, בְּהָם follows the direct object וְאֶת הַזּוּזִים and supplies the location of their defeat.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 14:5 pairs each defeated people with a location introduced by בְּ. The Rephaim are at Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim at Ham, and the Emim at Shaveh-kiriathaim.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition בְּ marks location. Its complement הָם is a proper place name.
analysis.sense: Ham, the place where the kings struck the Zuzim

draft.change: Add Genesis 14:5 as evidence for the existing definite-object sense of the particle at word index 0.
draft.definition: אֵת introduces the particular person or thing a verb acts on. It can recur before each of several coordinated objects.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 14:5, וְאֵת introduces הָאֵימִים as the third object of וַיַּכּוּ, after the Rephaim and the Zuzim.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 14:5, וַיַּכּוּ “they struck” governs three groups in succession. After אֶת רְפָאִים and וְאֶת הַזּוּזִים, וְאֵת הָאֵימִים adds the Emim as the third group struck.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” The unsuffixed particle אֵת marks the following noun phrase as a direct object.
analysis.sense: Marks the Emim as a definite direct object of “they struck.”

analysis.evidence: וְאֵת marks הָאֵימִים as the third direct object of וַיַּכּוּ, “they struck.” The Emites are listed alongside the Rephaim and the Zuzim, each with a place of defeat. Here the word names a people.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine plural gentilic noun in the absolute state. The ending ־ִים marks the plural.

analysis.evidence: Just as בְּהָם gives the site where the kings struck the Zuzim, בְּשָׁוֵה קִרְיָתָיִם gives the site where they struck the Emim. The two words together name the place Shaveh-kiriathaim.
analysis.morphology: The locative preposition בְּ prefixes the place name שָׁוֵה, the first element of שָׁוֵה קִרְיָתָיִם.
